# A field a literal omits carries its declared default into every target, not
# just the interpreter. The defaults were materialized in the interpreter only,
# so `color{r=255}` reached Go with no alpha and an opaque red rendered as
# #ff000000 once hex() started honoring alpha.

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=outjs app.sngl
grep 'x: 7' outjs/index.html
grep 'a: 255' outjs/index.html

[!exec:go] skip 'go toolchain required'
sngl build --lang=go --platform=bubbletea --opt name=sd bt.sngl
[toolchain] exists sd

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

struct P {
    x int = 7
    y int = 0
}

component main node {
    var p P = {y = 1}
    var c color = color{r = 255, g = 0, b = 0}
    text(value="{p.x}{c.hex()}")
}

window {
    main
}
-- bt.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output { go { bubbletea } }

struct P {
    x int = 7
    y int = 0
}

component main node {
    var p P = {y = 1}
    var c color = color{r = 255, g = 0, b = 0}
    text(value="{p.x}{c.hex()}")
}

window {
    main
}
-- testrun/build/bubbletea/go/bt.sngl/1 --
